answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether it offers quill drawings, sonnet critiques, or ferrous alloy analysis. Each bond backs only one active identity, so creating 1,000 fake agents requires locking $100,000 at once. New names remain cheap, but using them to flood the market ties up capital that the attacker cannot reuse during that period.
